basics.name: Omkar Patil
basics.label: CS PhD @ ASU
basics.summary: I completed my Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees at IIT Madras, where I built a strong foundation in robotics and machine learning. I am currently pursuing my Ph.D. at Arizona State University (ASU) in Dr. Nakul Gopalan’s lab, focusing on robot learning, particularly methods that leverage compositionality to build generalizable manipulation skills.

education.studyType: Bachelor's in Mechanical Engineering and Master's in Robotics and AI

publications.name: Self-Supervised Keyframe Discovery for Horizon-Invariant Behavior Cloning
publications.publisher: NeurIPS 2026 | Prabin Kumar Rath, Omkar Patil, Nakul Gopalan
publications.summary: Self-supervised method that discovers information-critical observations (mnemonics) as keyframes, conditioning behavior cloning policies on them to retain context over long horizons, without annotations.

publications.name: You've Got a Golden Ticket: Improving Generative Robot Policies With A Single Noise Vector
publications.publisher: arXiv | Omkar Patil, Ondrej Biza, Thomas Weng, Karl Schmeckpeper, Wil Thomason, Xiaohan Zhang, Kausik Sivakumar, Robin Walters, Nakul Gopalan, Sebastian Castro, Stephen Hart, Eric Rosen
publications.summary: Search method to find a single constant noise vector (golden ticket) that improves pretrained diffusion/flow matching robot policies including VLAs (GR00T N1.5, π0, SmolVLA) without any retraining.

publications.name: StageCraft: Execution Aware Mitigation of Distractor and Obstruction Failures in VLA Models
publications.publisher: IROS 2026 | Kartikay Pangaonkar*, Prabin Rath*, Omkar Patil*, Nakul Gopalan
publications.summary: Training-free VLM-based scene staging for VLAs (π0.5, SmolVLA); +40% absolute success on real robots.

publications.name: Factorizing Diffusion Policies for Observation Modality Prioritization
publications.publisher: ICRA 2026 | Omkar Patil, Prabin Rath, Kartikay Pangaonkar, Eric Rosen, Nakul Gopalan
publications.summary: Method to prioritize observational modalities, such as vision over tactile, for learning diffusion policies.

work.company: Logos Robotics Lab, Arizona State University
work.name: Logos Robotics Lab, Arizona State University
highlights: Build ROS 2 teleoperation pipelines (leader arm, VR headset) for a Franka Research 3 arm and a ROBOTIS AI Worker semi-humanoid, used to collect 500+ demonstrations across 10 tasks.
Build data-collection and real-time inference pipelines to deploy trained policies, including Diffusion Policy, ACT, and VLAs (π0.5, SmolVLA), on real robots.
Fine-tune policies with behavior cloning and on-robot policy improvement, and deploy simulation-trained policies on hardware (sim-to-real) for research experiments and demonstrations.
work.summary: PhD research on robot learning for real-world manipulation with Dr. Nakul Gopalan.

work.name: RAI Institute
highlights: Developed a latent-steering-based approach that improved generative policies on 46 of 51 tasks without retraining, resulting in the filing of a patent and a publication: https://lottery-tickets.rai-inst.com/.

Demonstrated that derivative-free episodic policy improvement can be competitive with policy-gradient and actor-critic methods, especially for VLAs, potentially with a 15× reduction in wall-clock time.
work.summary: Post-training of VLAs and generative robot policies on downstream reward functions.

work.name: Wells Fargo
highlights: Developed a novel metric to evaluate the quality of LLM-generated paraphrases ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.13119), [patent](https://patents.google.com/patent/US12524612B1/en)).
Surveyed and built LLM-enabled document generation, speeding up internal documentation ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.09341)).
